hero.body: D8 takes on hard problems and ships things that work, from concept to deployment. We develop real engineering solutions across multidisciplinary fields and different industries. Bring it on — it will ship out to D8 Standards.

services.title: Hardware & Software
services.description: Most vendors do one side. D8 does both, in one team, without the integration tax. From PCB to cloud dashboard, we own the full hardware-software stack and eliminate the gaps between layers.
capabilities: Firmware development for ESP32, STM32, and RTOS environments
PCB design, board bringup, and manufacturing handoff
Cloud connectivity, device management, and real-time data

services.title: Web & App
services.description: Platforms that operate, not just display. Scheduling, billing, multi-tenant data, the systems that run a business day to day. Built to scale and maintained by a team that understands the architecture.
capabilities: Web applications and multi-tenant SaaS platforms
Role-based access, billing, and operational workflows
API design, integrations, and service architecture
Mobile applications and progressive web apps

services.title: AI & Data
services.description: Not a wrapper around an existing model. Real inference pipelines, edge deployment, and data systems built for the questions you actually need to answer. We train, deploy, and keep models useful over time.
capabilities: Model training, fine-tuning, and performance evaluation
Edge inference on low-power hardware (Raspberry Pi, ESP32)
Data pipelines, ETL processes, and warehouse design

services.title: R&D
services.description: Research and Development — we go first. When a problem is undefined or the technology to solve it doesn't yet exist, we build the evidence that makes the next decision possible. D8 takes on ambiguous work and delivers something you can build on.

about.heading: We don't reinvent the wheel. We combine the ones already spinning to move something that never could before.
about.body1: D8 is a product engineering startup. We scan industries where existing solutions are fragmented, overpriced, or simply missing. We build what should exist. Our own products and client work are held to the same standard: if it ships from D8, it works.
about.body2: We operate across R&D, hardware and embedded systems, web and app development, and AI, in one team, without the handoffs or coordination overhead of managing multiple vendors. Most projects touch more than one domain. That's by design.
about.body3: The name is the philosophy: D8 is Day 8. After the seven days of creation, Day 8 is when humans start building on what already exists: not reinventing, but synthesizing and advancing. That's how we work.

industries.heading: How we build.
industries.body: Every project starts with research, not assumptions. From there we model the system, design the artifact, and validate it in the real world.

process.name: Research
process.desc: Map what exists, identify the gaps, and explore possible approaches before writing a line of code or cutting a trace.

process.name: Model
process.desc: Feasibility, architecture, and system planning. Define what gets built and how the pieces fit.

process.name: Design
process.desc: Schematics, UX, hardware layouts, and detailed technical specification.

process.name: Prototype
process.desc: Build, validate in the field, iterate, and hand off to deployment.

industries.name: Transit revenue collection system
industries.description: A bus fleet needed to collect, record, and report fare revenue without relying on manual cash handling. We researched existing fare collection systems, mapped the hardware constraints of a bus environment, and designed a custom unit from the ground up. The unit handles bill and coin intake, tamper-resistant storage, and real-time reporting to a cloud operations platform. The platform tracks fleet-wide revenue, flags anomalies, and generates the financial reports the company actually uses.

industries.name: Personal services booking platform
industries.description: Independent service businesses were running client relationships through spreadsheets, phone calls, and group chats. We studied how bookings, loyalty, and client history actually work in these operations, then designed a multi-tenant platform that handles all of it. Clients browse local businesses, book services, view their history, and activate recurring benefits. Owners manage their schedule, catalog, and client base from a single interface. The platform operates as a local discovery network across businesses, not just a back-office tool.

industries.name: Residential community management platform
industries.description: Gated community administrators were managing payments, visitor access, amenity reservations, and resident communications across disconnected tools — or none at all. We mapped the full administrative workflow, then built a multi-tenant platform where residents and administrators share one system with role-appropriate views. Residents pay fees, reserve amenities, register visitors, and receive community updates. Administrators manage the building, approve requests, and keep records without paper.

industries.name: Regulatory filing automation bot
industries.description: Accountants handling large client portfolios spent hours per client per period manually navigating government portals to file tax declarations. We analyzed the filing workflows for multiple declaration types, mapped the data inputs, and built an automation system that aggregates client financial data and submits completed filings without human intervention. Sold to accounting firms, it eliminates the repetitive document layer so accountants can focus on advisory work.

industries.name: Padel court scoring system
industries.description: Padel clubs had no reliable way to track live match scores on casual courts, forcing players to keep score in their heads or lose track entirely. We researched existing solutions, found them either too expensive or too fragile for daily club use, and built our own. Pressure sensors mounted on court walls detect wall strikes in real time. A companion display shows the live score, tracks game history, and supports multiple formats including pozos rotation for club nights. The system installs on existing courts without structural modification.

careers.heading2: We want people who want that.
careers.body: D8 is a small team with a wide scope: hardware, software, AI, and the R&D that connects them. We don't have career ladders or quarterly OKRs. We have problems that need solving and the autonomy to solve them.

principles.name: Ownership over permission
principles.desc: Everyone at D8 owns something real. Not a ticket queue: a problem. You define the approach, you make it work, you see it deployed. If you need someone to tell you what to do next, this isn't the place.

principles.name: We go all in on
principles.desc: We go as deep as the problem requires. We don't stop at 'working'; we stop at 'correct, robust, and fast'. Curiosity isn't a nice-to-have, it's the job.

principles.name: No handoffs
principles.desc: Hardware talks to firmware. Firmware talks to the cloud. The cloud talks to the UI. You'll understand the full stack, even the parts that aren't yours. That's how you build things that actually work.

principles.name: Credentials optional. Mediocrity isn't.
principles.desc: We don't care about degrees or years of experience. Self-taught, still in school, switching fields, all welcome. We care about how you think, how you learn, and how you handle being wrong. Someone who ships beats someone who coasts, every time.

founders.heading: The engineers behind the D8 Standard.

list.name: Nadir Alfaro
list.bio: Mechatronics engineer from the Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica. Defended a robotics thesis at TUM's ICS lab in Munich, then continued research across MEMS and NEMS groups at the same university. In the United States, he joined Amazon's automation division, building and commissioning large-scale conveyor systems for supply centers from the ground up. Those years abroad answered a question he hadn't fully formed: if a Costa Rican engineer can operate at that level out there, the talent was never the problem. D8 is what happens when you stop sending it elsewhere and start investing in ourselves.

list.name: This could be you.
list.bio: At D8 we don't hire employees — we invite associates. People who understand the D8 philosophy and want to keep advancing it. The deal is simple: if we do well, you do well. If you do well, we do well. There are no founder privileges here. We're all at the same level. What matters is what you build.

cta.heading: Have something to build?
cta.body: We work with companies who need a technical partner, not just a vendor. If you have a hard problem, we're interested.
